title: One singular-point blowup of a curve dominated by a regular birational cover
statement: Let $C$ and $R$ be integral Noetherian schemes of dimension $1$, let $R$ be regular, and let $r:R\to C$ be a finite morphism inducing an isomorphism $k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(R)$. Let $c\in C$ be a closed point whose local ring is not regular. Let $\mathcal I_c$ be the ideal sheaf of the reduced closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)\hookrightarrow C$, and put $b:C^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_c}C\to C$. Then $C^+$ is integral and Noetherian of dimension $1$, $b$ is finite and induces an isomorphism of function fields, and $b$ is not an isomorphism. There is a finite morphism $r^+:R\to C^+$ inducing an isomorphism of function fields and satisfying $b\circ r^+=r$.
